context: A teacher walks a uni student through a disaster-policy paper
purpose: Teach: 分裂/火災/津波/飛躍/流動/機動/抑圧/繁栄

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 論文、津波対策と都市の繁栄の関係を扱うんですね。
lines.en: Your thesis is on tsunami countermeasures and urban development, then?
lines.style: Warm, genuinely curious. Opens with a slight lift. Clear eye contact. Not rushing to fill the thought—letting him respond at his own pace.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。沿岸地域の流動的な人口にも触れたいです。
lines.en: Yes. I also want to address how coastal populations shift and flow.
lines.style: Careful, thinking-aloud quality. Slight hesitation before 'also'—showing he's still forming his thoughts. Soft but present. Not defensive.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 災害時の機動的な対応、火災と津波で異なる構造ですね。
lines.en: Emergency response is handled differently for fires versus tsunami—the structures diverge.
lines.style: Leaning forward slightly. A light tap of realization on the word 'diverge'. Pacing slows on the technical point to ensure it lands. Genuinely interested in his thesis.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 政策が分裂気味だった時期も、論じる予定です。
lines.en: There were periods when policy became fragmented too, so I'm planning to cover that.
lines.style: Growing surer in tone. Speaks with the quiet confidence of someone who's done the reading. Still respectful of her position, but not deferring unnecessarily.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 技術の飛躍が、抑圧的な行政運用を変えた事例もあります。
lines.en: There are cases where technological breakthroughs actually shifted how rigid bureaucracies operated.
lines.style: Offering the thought gently, as a mirror. Pace is unhurried—this is a suggestion, not a directive. A teacher's gift of a thread to follow.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 参考にします。来週、構成案をお持ちします。
lines.en: I'll definitely look into those. I'll bring you an outline next week.
lines.style: Nod in his voice. Genuine appreciation without overdoing it. Warm closure—not rushed, but ready to move on. A small smile underneath.
